newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to offload shares of 15 companies.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to offload shares of 15 companies.

text.p: Bangladesh will offload shares of 15 companies, including three multinationals, in the 1996/97 financial year (July-June), the chief of Bangladesh's Privatisation Board said on Tuesday.

The shares will be offered to the public in phases in consultation with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the state-owned Investment Corporation of Bangladesh, official BSS news agency quoted M. Matiur Rahman, the chairman of the board, as saying.
Besides, Rahman said, the government would sell 41 public companies also in the current year as part of its privatisation programme.
International tenders have already been floated to sell eight companies, he said.
"The government is firmly proceeding with the disinvestment programme. We are working hard on it," the board chairman said.

The companies from which the government will withdraw shares are: Metalex Corp, Bangladesh Can Company, Atlas Bangladesh Ltd, National Tubes, Lira Industrial Enterprises, Usmania Glass Sheet Factory, Zeal Bangla Sugar Mills, ARCO Industries, SAF Industries, Tigerwire Products, National Iron & Steel and Mirpur Ceramic.
The multinationals are Reckitt & Colman, Berger (Bangladesh) Ltd, and Siemens Ltd. Of the 15, six are listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange.
Rahman said 10.65 percent of the Reckitt & Colman shares, 42.33 of Berger stocks and 31.66 of the Siemens shares would be sold.
